scope: R125 measurements of every user-approved lossy acceleration candidate, each measured against the accepted FA base with the identical R124 inputs. Numbers are reported for the user to decide; nothing here is auto-accepted.

candidates.candidate: VAE Half decoder parameters + native fused decoder fast path
candidates.classification: REJECT on performance: no measurable gain
candidates.how: the R124 hook forces original FP32 VAE parameters and skips the whole installer; setting H3_NPU_VAE_PRESERVE_FP32_PARAMS124=0 restores the native installer

speed.verdict: decode improves by at most 4 percent, which is inside run-to-run variance, and the end-to-end wall is unchanged

candidates.conclusion: The VAE decode time is not dominated by decoder parameter precision. Something else (tile staging / temporal streaming / audio decode) owns those ~132 s, so the Half-parameter rewrite buys nothing and is not worth its numerical risk.

candidates.how: module-level _modulate_gate narrowed to the incoming Half dtype, so the 50-block residual stream stops being widened to FP32; the 2-layer token refiner keeps FP32 accumulation, so this is a lower bound on a full rewrite

speed.verdict: about 40 percent slower than the FA base

numerics.verdict: numerically indistinguishable from the FA base

candidates.conclusion: The FP32 residual accumulation is not a speed cost in this graph and dropping it changes nothing measurable, so the candidate adds risk for negative benefit.

candidates.candidate: fused FP16 pointwise kernels, measured via the SwiGLU product (platform SiluAndMul)
candidates.classification: REJECT on performance and numerics: no gain, and drift accumulates
candidates.how: MiniMaxH3MLP.forward replaces F.silu(gate.float()) * up.float() with the platform SiluAndMul so the gate product is computed in FP16 in one pass

numerics.verdict: 2-4x the FA base on video and up to 16x on audio by step 48; the drift grows with step index

candidates.conclusion: Fusing the gate product removes the FP32 guard on the largest pointwise tensor and buys no time, so it is worse on both axes.

candidates.candidate: raised tensor/sequence parallelism to make the DiT resident
candidates.classification: NOT AVAILABLE at the baseline precision configuration

measured.resident_attempt: NPU OOM, 31.06 GiB allocated and a 404 MiB request failed on all 8 ranks
measured.evidence: per-rank parameter bytes identical at TP2 and TP8 (33168334080 bytes)

candidates.conclusion: The DiT is fully replicated per rank and only sequence parallelism splits activations, so residency cannot fit 32 GiB and raising TP does not reduce per-rank weights. Sequence parallelism beyond USP4 is slower, so the best measured layout stays TP2/USP4.

rejected_reasons: VAE fast path: no decode or wall gain
fused SwiGLU: no gain and accumulating numeric drift
net_result.remaining_bottleneck: With attention fixed, one warm step is dominated by per-block weight staging from the CPU offload (the DiT cannot be resident at this precision configuration), which is why residency-free candidates such as pointwise fusion and residual-narrowing did nothing.

targets_still_unmet.encoder_under_2s: not met (R124 live encoder stage about 65 s)
targets_still_unmet.DiT_under_15s_per_step: not met, but now close: 17.76 s in the engine and 18.41 s in the replay harness
targets_still_unmet.VAE_decode_under_20s: not met (about 132-139 s, and the fast path does not move it)

no_claim: No universal picture or audio quality claim; the audio track stays at about -75 dBFS in every configuration and sample-level audio differences are not used as evidence.
No lossy candidate other than the FA kernel was enabled anywhere.
No claim that the original performance goal is complete.
